answer: Because the gale liability is recorded in the basalt ledger at admission, the canyon audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 66% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 10 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
